Transformer 需要位置编码，是因为其自注意力模块具有置换不变性。
仅使用注意力机制无法捕捉序列中的顺序关系，会退化为"词袋模型"。
需要引入位置编码（Position Embedding, PE）对序列信息进行精确建模，把绝对或相对位置信息整合到模型中。
由于 Transformer 的编码器结构本身无法识别序列中元素的顺序，位置编码（Position Embedding, PE）被引入来表示序列中的位置信息。
给定一个词元 ut，位置编码根据其在输入中的绝对位置分配一个固定长度的嵌入向量 pt∈RH。
每个词元对应的词向量和位置向量直接相加，生成最终的输入嵌入序列 xt = vt + pt。
原始的 Transformer 采用了正余弦位置编码，在不同维度上预先定义特定的正弦或余弦函数。
正余弦位置编码第 i 维的值按 sin(t/10000^(i−2)/H)（i mod 2 = 0）或 cos(t/10000^(i−1)/H)（i mod 2 = 1）设置。
绝对位置编码只能局限于建模训练样本中出现的位置，无法建模训练数据中未出现过的位置，因此极大地限制了它们处理长文本的能力。
相对位置编码则根据键和查询之间的偏移量计算，通常应用于注意力矩阵的计算中，而不是直接与词元本身的位置编码相加。
应用相对位置编码的模型常具备一定的外推能力。

一旦机器学习系统被用于（部分或完全）自动化决策，评估视野就从"预测"扩展到"决策"，此时精度很少成为合适的衡量标准。
部署机器学习系统时，不仅仅是在优化一个预测模型，而通常是在提供一个会被用来（部分或完全）进行自动化决策的工具。
这些技术系统可能会通过其进行的决定而影响到每个人的生活。
从考虑预测到决策的飞跃不仅提出了新的技术问题，还提出了一系列必须仔细考虑的伦理问题。
一旦我们规划整个决策系统，就必须退后一步重新考虑如何评估我们的技术。
在视野变化所导致的结果中，我们会发现精度很少成为合适的衡量标准。
当我们将预测转化为行动时，我们通常会考虑到各种方式犯错的潜在成本敏感性。
将图像错误地分到某一类别可能被视为种族歧视，而错误地分到另一个类别是无害的，那么可能需要相应地调整阈值，在设计决策方式时考虑这些社会价值。
我们还需要注意预测系统如何导致反馈循环。
预测性警务系统将巡逻人员分配到预测犯罪率较高的地区，会形成犯罪率高的社区得到更多巡逻、发现更多犯罪行为、模型预测更多犯罪、下一次迭代更倾向针对同一地区的模式，研究人员称之为"失控反馈循环"。
我们首先要注意我们是否解决了正确的问题。
不均衡或缺乏代表性的数据集会使模型产生偏见。
皮肤癌识别模型从未"见过"黑色皮肤的人群就会束手无策。
用"过去的招聘决策数据"训练简历筛选模型可能无意中捕捉到历史残留的不公正并将其自动化。
在预测性监管、简历筛选和用于贷款的风险模型等敏感应用中，必须特别警惕垃圾数据带来的后果。

Under annual compounding the average of the individual growth rates does not equal the overall growth rate.
Continuous growth rates can be averaged directly because they are differences of natural logarithms that telescope and cancel out.
Under continuous compounding, computing the growth rate between two values of a series requires nothing more than taking the difference of their natural logarithms.

Continuous growth rates have the desirable property that if you compute the year-by-year continuous growth rates of a series and then take the average of those rates, the result is equal to the continuous growth rate over the entire interval.
For the GDP values $100K, $130K, $135K, the continuous growth rate between the first two is ln($130K) − ln($100K), and between the second two is ln($135K) − ln($130K).

The average of the two continuous growth rates is [ln($135K) − ln($130K) + ln($130K) − ln($100K)] / 2, and the two ln($130K) terms cancel, leaving exactly the formula for the continuous growth rate between the first and third values.
If we carry out the same exercise under simple growth or annually compounded growth, the average of the individual growth rates will not equal the overall growth rate.
If GDP grows by 8% this year and 4% next year, both calculated using annual compounding, then the two-year growth rate will not be 6% (it will actually be 5.98%).
If the 8% and 4% numbers were calculated using continuous compounding, then the continuous growth rate over the two-year period would be 6%.

The Viterbi algorithm has three steps that fill the probability lattice: initialization, recursion, and termination.
Initialization fills the first column with πs ∗ bs(o1).
Recursion fills each later cell by taking the max over previous states.
Termination takes the max over the final column to get the best path probability and backpointer.
In the initialization step, for each state s from 1 to N, viterbi[s,1] ← πs ∗ bs(o1) and backpointer[s,1] ← 0.
In the recursion step, for each time step t from 2 to T and each state s from 1 to N, viterbi[s,t] ← max over s′ of viterbi[s′,t−1] ∗ as′,s ∗ bs(ot).
In the recursion step, backpointer[s,t] ← argmax over s′ of viterbi[s′,t−1] ∗ as′,s ∗ bs(ot).
In the termination step, bestpathprob ← max over s of viterbi[s,T].
In the termination step, bestpathpointer ← argmax over s of viterbi[s,T].
The best path starts at bestpathpointer and follows backpointer[] to states back in time.

In terms of the lattice, each cell vt(j) represents the probability that the HMM is in state j after seeing the first t observations and passing through the most probable state sequence q1,...,qt−1, given the HMM λ.
The recursion fills each cell as vt(j) = max over i of vt−1(i) aij bj(ot).
The recursion takes the most probable of the extensions of the paths that lead to the current cell.

rt(θ) = πθ(at|st)/πθold(at|st)（公式8.19）。
PPO 选取裁剪前后的优势值的最小值参与优化。

A language L is decided in polynomial time by an algorithm A if there exists a constant k such that for any length-n string x ∈ {0,1}*, the algorithm correctly decides whether x ∈ L in time O(n^k).
To accept a language, an algorithm need only produce an answer when provided a string in L.
To decide a language, an algorithm must correctly accept or reject every string in {0,1}*.

A complexity class is informally defined as a set of languages, membership in which is determined by a complexity measure, such as running time, of an algorithm that determines whether a given string x belongs to language L.
Theorem 34.2: P = {L : L is accepted by a polynomial-time algorithm}.

The language-theoretic definition corresponds to the earlier definition of P as the set of concrete decision problems that are polynomial-time solvable, i.e., solvable in time O(n^k) for some constant k.

In a bigram language model, P(wn|wn−1) is estimated by MLE.
MLE estimation of P(wn|wn−1) takes the count of the bigram C(wn−1wn) and normalizes it by the sum of all bigram counts that share the same first word wn−1.
The normalization of the bigram count simplifies to dividing by the unigram count C(wn−1): P(wn|wn−1) = C(wn−1wn) / C(wn−1) (Eq. 3.11).
Each sentence is augmented with <s> at the beginning to give the bigram context of the first word.
Each sentence is augmented with </s> at the end to make the bigram grammar a true probability distribution.

Without an end-symbol, instead of the sentence probabilities of all sentences summing to one, the sentence probabilities for all sentences of a given length would sum to one, defining an infinite set of probability distributions, one per sentence length.
MLE gets the estimate for n-gram model parameters by getting counts from a corpus and normalizing the counts so that they lie between 0 and 1.
Normalizing means dividing by some total count so that the resulting probabilities fall between 0 and 1 and sum to 1.

To compute a particular bigram probability of a word wn given a previous word wn−1, compute the count of the bigram C(wn−1wn) and normalize by the sum of all the bigrams that share the same first word wn−1: P(wn|wn−1) = C(wn−1wn) / Σw C(wn−1w) (Eq. 3.10).
The sum of all bigram counts that start with a given word wn−1 must be equal to the unigram count for that word wn−1.
The general case of MLE N-gram parameter estimation (N = 2,3,...) is P(wn|wn−N+1:n−1) = C(wn−N+1:n−1 wn) / C(wn−N+1:n−1) (Eq. 3.12).

The feedforward layer is called position-wise because it operates on each token position i independently.
The attention network's job is to mix information from different token positions.
The feedforward layer's weights are shared across positions, meaning the same parameters are applied to every token position.
The feedforward layer's weights are different from layer to layer.
The feedforward layer is a fully-connected 2-layer network, i.e., one hidden layer and two weight matrices.
It is common to make the hidden-layer dimensionality dff be 4 times larger than the model dimensionality d.
In the original transformer model, d = 512 and dff = 2048.

Because the feedforward networks have most of the parameters of the transformers, these parameters seem to encode most of the factual knowledge in the transformer (Geva et al., 2021; Meng et al., 2022).
Most LLMs now use gated feedforward layers with the SwiGLU activation.
FFNSwiGLU(x,W1,W2,W3,b1,b2,b3,β) = Swishβ(xW1+b1) ⊗ (xW2+b2) W3+b3.

在 Elo 评分体系中，模型 A 的期望胜率由两个模型当前 Elo 分数之差计算：EA = 1/(1+10^((rB−rA)/400))（公式12.13）。
在 Elo 评分体系中，模型 B 的期望胜率为 EB = 1/(1+10^((rA−rB)/400))（公式12.14）。
在 Elo 评分体系中，rA、rB 分别代表模型 A 和模型 B 的当前 Elo 分数。
Elo 评分体系的核心思想是通过模型之间的成对比较来动态更新两个模型各自的评分。
在 Elo 评分体系中，首先为每个模型分配一个初始 Elo 分数。
在进行模型比较时，根据两个模型当前的 Elo 分数计算出它们各自的期望胜率（p.295）。
随后根据实际的比较结果更新 Elo 分数：r′A = rA + K×(SA−EA)（公式12.15）。
在公式 r′A = rA + K×(SA−EA) 中，K 是调整系数，决定比较结果对 Elo 分数更新的影响程度。
在公式 r′A = rA + K×(SA−EA) 中，SA 表示模型 A 的实际得分（通常 1 表示胜利、0.5 表示平局、0 表示失败）。
在公式 r′A = rA + K×(SA−EA) 中，EA 是模型 A 的期望胜率（p.295）。
Elo 评分系统假设每个模型输出都有一个 Elo 等级分，可用于估计该输出获胜的概率。
在 Elo 评分系统的两两对决中，若某输出获胜（标注员更喜欢该输出），其等级分上升，反之下降。
在 Elo 评分系统的两两对决中，等级分的升降幅度取决于预估获胜概率与实际胜负情况（p.184）。
A dependency structure is represented as a directed graph G = (V, A).
V is the set of vertices, and A is the set of arcs, i.e. ordered pairs of vertices.
A dependency structure can be represented as a directed graph G = (V,A), consisting of a set of vertices V, and a set of ordered pairs of vertices A, which are called arcs.
For the most part, the set of vertices, V, corresponds exactly to the set of words in a given sentence.
The set of vertices might also correspond to punctuation.
When dealing with morphologically complex languages, the set of vertices might consist of stems and affixes.
The set of arcs, A, captures the head-dependent and grammatical function relationships between the elements in V.
Frequent restrictions on dependency structures are that they must be connected, have a designated root node, and be acyclic or planar.
A dependency tree is a directed graph with a single designated root node that has no incoming arcs.
In a dependency tree, each non-root vertex has exactly one incoming arc.
In a dependency tree, there is a unique path from the root node to each vertex in V.

To prove that the greedy algorithm HUFFMAN is correct, one shows that the problem of determining an optimal prefix code exhibits the greedy-choice and optimal-substructure properties (p.454).
The proof of HUFFMAN's correctness follows from two lemmas and a theorem.
Greedy-choice property — Lemma 16.2 (p.454): Let C be an alphabet in which each character c has frequency c.freq, and let x and y be two characters in C having the lowest frequencies.
Then there exists an optimal prefix code for C in which the codewords for x and y have the same length and differ only in the last bit.

Proof idea for Lemma 16.2: take the tree T representing an arbitrary optimal prefix code and modify it to make a tree representing another optimal prefix code such that x and y appear as sibling leaves of maximum depth in the new tree; then the codewords for x and y will have the same length and differ only in the last bit.

Concretely, let a and b be two characters that are sibling leaves of maximum depth in T, assume a.freq ≤ b.freq and x.freq ≤ y.freq, so x.freq ≤ a.freq and y.freq ≤ b.freq; exchange the positions in T of a and x to produce T′, and then exchange the positions in T′ of b and y to produce T″ (p.454).
Optimal-substructure property — Lemma 16.3 (p.456): Let C be a given alphabet with frequency c.freq defined for each character c in C.
Let x and y be two characters in C with minimum frequency.
Let C′ be the alphabet C with the characters x and y removed and a new character z added, so that C′ = C − {x, y} ∪ {z}.
Define freq for C′ as for C, except that z.freq = x.freq + y.freq.
Let T′ be any tree representing an optimal prefix code for the alphabet C′.
Then the tree T, obtained from T′ by replacing the leaf node for z with an internal node having x and y as children, represents an optimal prefix code for the alphabet C.

Proof of Lemma 16.3: for each character c in C − {x, y}, d_T(c) = d_T′(c); since d_T(x) = d_T(y) = d_T′(z) + 1, we get x.freq·d_T(x) + y.freq·d_T(y) = (x.freq + y.freq)·(d_T′(z) + 1) = z.freq·d_T′(z) + (x.freq + y.freq), from which B(T) = B(T′) + x.freq + y.freq, or equivalently B(T′) = B(T) − x.freq − y.freq.

The lemma is then proved by contradiction: if T were not optimal for C, there would exist an optimal tree T″ with B(T″) < B(T) (having x and y as siblings, by Lemma 16.2); letting T′′′ be T″ with the common parent of x and y replaced by a leaf z with z.freq = x.freq + y.freq gives B(T′′′) = B(T″) − x.freq − y.freq < B(T) − x.freq − y.freq = B(T′), contradicting the optimality of T′ (p.456).
Theorem 16.4 (p.456): Procedure HUFFMAN produces an optimal prefix code.
Proof of Theorem 16.4: Immediate from Lemmas 16.2 and 16.3.
Background: the cost of a tree is B(T) = Σ_{c∈C} c.freq · d_T(c), where d_T(c) is the depth of c's leaf in the tree and also the length of the codeword for character c (p.452).
